reader.requirement: At --std 85 the RECORD DELIMITER clause (either STANDARD-1 or implementor-name-1) may be written only for a file whose records are variable length (RECORD IS VARYING; a Format 1 RECORD CONTAINS n CHARACTERS file is explicitly fixed, a file with no RECORD clause or Format 3 is implementor-defined), so the clause on an explicitly fixed file is not conforming source.
reader.edition-search: Read FileControlBinder.BindFileControl's recordDelimiterClause arm and EditionContext.Declined (severity of the descriptor and --permissive only; no edition test). Grepped src for RecordDelimiter/recordDelimiterClause: FileControlKeyRules (Format 3 organization rule), FileEntryIdentity (external connector identity) and FileModel; none consults the edition. rd1.cob gives the same three COBOL1778 warnings and the same output at --std 85 and --std 2023.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb292_record_delimiter_witness writes the clause only on RECORD IS VARYING files (the legal half); the clause on an explicitly fixed (Format 1 RECORD clause) file, the half SR1 forbids, is not exercised

probes.printed: warning COBOL1778 on FV (VARYING, STANDARD-1), FF (RECORD CONTAINS 10 CHARACTERS, STANDARD-1) and FN (RECORD CONTAINS 10 CHARACTERS, MYDELIM); EXIT 0; '03 ABC 0123456789 XYZ'
probes.expected: FF and FN violate SR1 (Format 1 is fixed length, §1985:II.2.1.4.1); the compiler gives the same decline warning as for the legal FV and does not name SR1

probes.printed: warning COBOL1778 and error COBOL2912: file 'FR' is RELATIVE, but its file control entry specifies the sequential format (a RECORD DELIMITER clause)
probes.expected: the 1985 clause is Sequential I-O only; a relative file entry refuses it

probes.printed: at --std 2023: 3 x warning COBOL1778, same output

reader.notes: The whole clause is declined accept-inert with COBOL1778 at every edition (docs/conformance/2/26.md, DOC-A.1-150; kb/Work PB292), and DiagnosticCatalog records the decision not to enforce SR1 inside the declined clause, citing §2023:4.2.6 para 3. DOUBT: at 1985 the licence is §1985:I.1.5.2.5.1 with §1985:C.3 item 6, which reaches the STANDARD-1 phrase only; 1985 has no sentence excusing syntax errors in unsupported syntax, so the implementor-name-1 arm on a fixed file (FN) is flagged only by the generic decline warning. Since this implementation defines no implementor-name, that arm is never conforming source and is warned; an adjudicator who wants SR1 named would rate it DIVERGES (under-rejects, cause c).
